interface.name: cosmic_session_hold_manager_v1

description.summary: hold back the reveal of a newly started session

interface.description:
When a session starts, the compositor briefly keeps the previous session's last frame on screen and cross-fades out of it once there is something to show. A client that intends to cover the session before the user sees it — a first-run experience, for instance — can use this to keep that frame up until it actually has pixels on screen.
The compositor never needs to know which client that is. Any client may claim a hold, and a client that decides it has nothing to show simply never claims one, so no configuration names any application.
Holds are only meaningful while a session is being revealed. Claiming one at any other time is harmless and does nothing.

request.name: destroy
hold

description.summary: keep the session hidden for now

request.description:
Ask the compositor not to reveal the session yet, because this client is about to put something on screen.
The reply to this is not an event: the caller should get on with showing whatever it intends to show, and release the hold once it is genuinely visible.
timeout_ms is how long the client believes it needs, as a hint. The compositor clamps it to its own limit, so a client cannot keep the session hidden indefinitely by asking for a large value, and a client that dies takes its hold with it.

arg.name: timeout_ms
arg.summary: how long the client expects to need

interface.name: cosmic_session_hold_v1

description.summary: an outstanding hold on revealing the session

interface.description: While this object is alive the compositor does not begin revealing the session. Destroying it, or disconnecting, releases the hold.

request.name: release
request.description: The client now has something on screen, or has given up trying. The compositor reveals the session unless another hold is outstanding.

event.name: expired
event.description: The compositor waited as long as it is willing to and has revealed the session. The hold no longer has any effect; the client should expect whatever it shows from now on to appear over an already-visible session. The object remains valid and should still be released.
